So, i am just curious to what yall believe.
If someone is harassed to the point of self harm or suicide should the person/people doing the harassment or bullying be charged with a crime?

No.

When you shoot somebody they're going to suffer substantial injury regardless of the person. When you call somebody a bad name it's going to do absolutely nothing to some people, others might go into fits of rage, others might go into an emo rage and start hurting themselves. The consequence of the action is largely dependent upon the victim. So while it may be appropriate to penalize the action, it should not necessarily be penalized in proportion to the response of the victim.

For a bad name, sure, but what about if you dialled it up to 11 (got them fired, caused their partner to leave them, caused them to lose their kids, etc.)? Couldn't there be a 'reasonable person' test? If you call a reasonable person a fuckwit, they're not going to top themselves, but if you completely fuck over their life they very well may.

The point is that any sort of penalization would need to be related to the action itself and not the consequences of that action since the consequences are going to vary radically dependent upon the mental state of the victim. So the crime would not be 'harassing to the point of self harm' but engaging in in a certain type of behavior. In fact this is already the law in the United States. We have some of the toughest laws on the books against online harassment:

Here is 18 U.S. Code § 2261A - Stalking :

Whoever— (1) travels in interstate or foreign commerce or is present within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States, or enters or leaves Indian country, with the intent to kill, injure, harass, intimidate, or place under surveillance with intent to kill, injure, harass, or intimidate another person, and in the course of, or as a result of, such travel or presence engages in conduct that—

(A) places that person in reasonable fear of the death of, or serious bodily injury to—

(i) that person;

(ii) an immediate family member (as defined in section 115) of that person; or

(iii) a spouse or intimate partner of that person; or

(B) causes, attempts to cause, or would be reasonably expected to cause substantial emotional distress to a person described in clause (i), (ii), or (iii) of subparagraph (A); or

(2) with the intent to kill, injure, harass, intimidate, or place under surveillance with intent to kill, injure, harass, or intimidate another person, uses the mail, any interactive computer service or electronic communication service or electronic communication system of interstate commerce, or any other facility of interstate or foreign commerce to engage in a course of conduct that—

(A) places that person in reasonable fear of the death of or serious bodily injury to a person described in clause (i), (ii), or (iii) of paragraph (1)(A); or

(B) causes, attempts to cause, or would be reasonably expected to cause substantial emotional distress to a person described in clause (i), (ii), or (iii) of paragraph (1)(A), shall be punished as provided in section 2261 (b) of this title.

Note that even engaging in behavior that would be reasonably expected to cause substantial emotional distress is a crime. But the law actually means what it says. You can't simply declare behavior you don't like as causing you substantial emotional distress. The courts for now are still fierce defenders of the first amendment and this law is certainly entering a bit of a grey area, but it is still the law for now. Here are some interesting legal opinions related to it actually related to first amendment appeals against it.
